source.note: The source is this repository's own Python implementation, not a second checkout. Cadenza is being rewritten in place (cadenza#8): `src/cadenza/` and `tests/` are the specification until a later PR retires them, so every inventory here is collected from the working tree at the recorded revision.

suite_baseline.reconciliation: `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` at a5672f8 on CPython 3.12.3: 330 passed. No module is skipped at collection time, so collected == the sum of the eight per-file inventories with nothing left over. See parity/source-inventory.manifest.json.

file.note: 35 test functions, 57 collected node ids: six functions are parametrized (a non-string kind over 4, an accepted URL over 4, each documented scheme over 3, other userinfo over 3, an embedded password over 2, whitespace/control characters in a URL over 3, NUL/control characters in a path over 3, a field beyond kind over 3, the canonical form over 3, urlsplit's own rejection over 2, a malformed port over 2, a well-formed port over 2).

systematic_mappings.to: `parse(table, options)` with the same three defaults, `options` an object rather than keyword arguments
systematic_mappings.why: A direct translation; TypeScript has no `**kwargs`, so the optional overrides move into one options object rather than trailing keyword arguments.

systematic_mappings.from: `pytest.raises(Kind, match=...) as caught`, then `caught.value` and, for two cases, `str(caught.value)` / `caught.value.location`
systematic_mappings.why: The same helper the composition belt's ledgers record, for the same reason: `expect(...).toThrow(...)` checks the class or the message but yields no instance, and this file's refusals go on to assert `.location` twice and the raw error text in every other case.
systematic_mappings.affects: the forty-five cases that assert a refusal

systematic_mappings.from: `tmp_path` (pytest's per-test filesystem fixture), and in one case `monkeypatch.setenv`
systematic_mappings.to: `CATALOG_DIR` / `ELSEWHERE` (absolute directories from `test/support.ts`) that touch no filesystem, and direct `process.env` mutation restored with `onTestFinished`
systematic_mappings.why: `parseCloneSource` never stats or reads a path (design doc section 3.1 -- it resolves `local_path` lexically, `normalisePath`/`_normalise_path` call `normpath`, never a filesystem-resolving call), so every case that took `tmp_path` needed only an absolute directory, not a real one. The precedent is the composition belt's `parity/compose.ledger.json` systematic mapping for the same substitution. `monkeypatch.setenv`, which has no vitest counterpart, becomes a direct `process.env.HOME`/`process.env.USERPROFILE` assignment registered for cleanup with `onTestFinished` at the point of acquisition (docs/porting.md's testkit rule 1), rather than a file-level `afterEach`.
systematic_mappings.affects: the thirteen local_path cases that took `tmp_path`, all marked `adapted`; see each entry's own reason

systematic_mappings.from: pytest's escaped node id spelling for a parametrised case whose value is a control character or an astral/non-ASCII code point -- `[web\x00repo]`, `[https://exa\u2100mple.com/r.git]`
systematic_mappings.to: the literal escaped text kept as the `parametrize()` id, with the actual code point only in the case's runtime value
systematic_mappings.why: `docs/porting.md` section 5's target id rule: the id is a byte-stable function of the source id, not of the runtime value, and the source id pytest actually printed is the ASCII-escaped spelling (`--collect-only` never emits a raw control character or an astral code point into a node id).
systematic_mappings.affects: the five cases with a control character or non-ASCII code point in their parametrised value

target_only_tests.why: Every case in this file translates a source case; nothing here needed a property with no source counterpart.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `expanduser` resolves a bare `~` and not `~user`: CPython consults the password database and, where the user is unknown, returns the path unchanged -- the branch this port always takes, because Node has no password database. No case in this file (nor in `tests/test_compose.py`, `tests/test_resolve.py` or `tests/test_toml_loader.py`) uses `~user`.
inherited_limitations.why: Recorded already at `src/domain/python-path.ts` and in `parity/compose.ledger.json`; repeated here because this is the belt whose own file states the `~` case (`test_tilde_is_expanded_against_the_home_directory`) and is therefore the natural place to also state what is deliberately not covered by it.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `urlsplit`'s bracketed-host check defers to `ipaddress.ip_address` in CPython and to `node:net`'s `isIP` in `src/domain/python-urlsplit.ts`. The two agree on ordinary addresses and may disagree at the edges -- a scoped or otherwise unusual IPv6 literal. No case in this file reaches that edge; `test_a_url_that_urlsplit_itself_rejects_is_a_typed_refusal`'s bracketed-host case (`https://[::1/repo.git`) is unbalanced, which both implementations refuse the same way, before either would consult the address parser.
inherited_limitations.why: Recorded already in `parity/compose.ledger.json` as an inherited limitation of `src/domain/python-urlsplit.ts`; repeated here because this is the belt whose file is `urlsplit`'s primary caller and closest cover, and the gap survives this belt closing.

entries.target_id: test/domain/clone-source.test.ts::local_path > a tilde is expanded against the home directory
entries.reason: Same assertion: a leading `~` expands against the home directory before anchoring. Adapted twice over: `monkeypatch.setenv` has no counterpart, so `process.env.HOME`/`process.env.USERPROFILE` are set directly and restored with `onTestFinished` at the point of acquisition (docs/porting.md rule 1); and `tmp_path` stands in for by `ELSEWHERE`, for the reason the previous two cases record. Both HOME and USERPROFILE are set because `ntpath.expanduser` ignores HOME entirely and reads USERPROFILE, so setting only HOME would assert nothing on the Windows cell -- the source's own comment.

entries.target_id: test/domain/clone-source.test.ts::canonical form > sources are frozen
entries.reason: Same property -- a source cannot be mutated after construction -- reached by a different mechanism. Python's `FrozenInstanceError` comes from a `@dataclass(frozen=True)`; a `CloneSource` here is a structural interface, so `gitUrlSource` freezes the object it returns with `Object.freeze`, and an ES module's implicit strict mode turns the assignment into a `TypeError` rather than a silent no-op. `# ts-expect-error` marks the assignment as a compile-time error too, so the case pins both halves of the guarantee: the type checker refuses it and the runtime refuses it.
